title: Restricting a right-fraction localization to a subcategory with enough denominators
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and $W$ a class of its morphisms containing identities and closed under composition. Assume the right-fraction axioms: for $f:X\to Z$ and $s:Y\to Z$ with $s\in W$ there are $t:T\to X$ in $W$ and $g:T\to Y$ with $ft=sg$; and whenever $f,g:X\to Y$ and $s:Y\to Z$ in $W$ satisfy $sf=sg$, there is $t:T\to X$ in $W$ with $ft=gt$. In the first axiom only $s$, not $f$, is required to lie in $W$. Let $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal C$ be a full subcategory, and assume that every $X\in\mathcal C$ admits an arrow $s:B\to X$ in $W$ with $B\in\mathcal B$. Put $W_{\mathcal B}=W\cap\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal B)$. Then $W_{\mathcal B}$ has a right calculus of fractions, and the inclusion induces an equivalence $\mathcal B[W_{\mathcal B}^{-1}]\to\mathcal C[W^{-1}]$, where localization is in the universal-property sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Categories and localizations are taken in a common larger universe. Neither a functorial choice of the arrows $B\to X$ nor a triangulated structure is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GSL (lemma-localization-subcategory), proof by refining right-fraction sources into the full subcategory. This is the categorical right-calculus form of that proof: replace its triangulated and saturation hypotheses by the stated right-fraction axioms; it is not the verbatim triangulated statement.

proof.text: Identities and composites in $W_{\mathcal B}$ remain identities and composites in $W$. For the right Ore axiom take $f:X\to Z$ and $s:Y\to Z$ in $\mathcal B$ with only $s\in W_{\mathcal B}$. The ambient axiom gives $t:T\to X$ in $W$ and $g:T\to Y$ with $f\circ t=s\circ g$. Choose $r:B_T\to T$ in $W$ with $B_T\in\mathcal B$. Then $t\circ r\in W$, and $f\circ t\circ r=s\circ g\circ r$. Fullness puts both $t\circ r$ and $g\circ r$ in $\mathcal B$, so these are the required restricted Ore square. This is a direct application of the hypotheses; $f$ need not be in $W$.

source.place: Tag 0GSL (lemma-localization-subcategory), categorical refinement argument; right-fraction axioms in Categories Tag 04VC (definition-multiplicative-system).

proof.text: For the cancellation axiom take $f,g:X\to Y$ and $s:Y\to Z$ in $\mathcal B$ with $s\in W_{\mathcal B}$ and $s\circ f=s\circ g$. Ambient cancellation gives $t:T\to X$ in $W$ with $f\circ t=g\circ t$. Choose $r:B_T\to T$ as in step 1. Then $t\circ r$ belongs to $W_{\mathcal B}$ and equalizes $f,g$. Together with step 1 this proves all the right-fraction axioms for $W_{\mathcal B}$.

source.place: Tag 0GSL (lemma-localization-subcategory), categorical refinement argument; right-fraction axioms in Categories Tag 04VC (definition-multiplicative-system).

proof.text: Write $i:\mathcal B\hookrightarrow\mathcal C$ for inclusion and let $Q_B:\mathcal B\to\mathcal L_B$, $Q_C:\mathcal C\to\mathcal L_C$ denote the indicated universal-property localizations. Since $Q_Ci$ inverts $W_{\mathcal B}$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](1) gives $F:\mathcal L_B\to\mathcal L_C$ and a natural isomorphism $\alpha:FQ_B\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_Ci$. For $X,Y\in\mathcal B$ put $H_{X,Y}(u)=\alpha_Y\circ F(u)\circ\alpha_X^{-1}$. Naturality and preservation of inverses give, for each roof $X\xleftarrow{s}P\xrightarrow{a}Y$ in $\mathcal B$, $$H_{X,Y}(Q_B(a)Q_B(s)^{-1})=Q_C(a)Q_C(s)^{-1}.$$ Thus bijectivity of $H_{X,Y}$ is precisely bijectivity of the corresponding Hom map of $F$.

source.place: Tag 04VK (lemma-properties-right-localization), factorization; natural-isomorphism formulation as in lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property.

proof.text: Fix $X,Y\in\mathcal B$ and $h:Q_C(X)\to Q_C(Y)$. By [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation] for $(\mathcal C,W,Q_C)$, write $h=Q_C(a)Q_C(s)^{-1}$ with $s:P\to X$ in $W$ and $a:P\to Y$. Choose $r:B_P\to P$ in $W$ with $B_P\in\mathcal B$. Both $s\circ r$ and $a\circ r$ are arrows in $\mathcal B$, and $s\circ r\in W_{\mathcal B}$. Inverting $Q_C(r)$ gives $$Q_C(a\circ r)Q_C(s\circ r)^{-1}=Q_C(a)Q_C(s)^{-1}=h.$$ The roof $(s\circ r,a\circ r)$ in $\mathcal B$ therefore supplies a preimage under $H_{X,Y}$ by step 3. This proves surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0GSL (lemma-localization-subcategory), categorical refinement argument; right-fraction axioms in Categories Tag 04VC (definition-multiplicative-system).

proof.text: For injectivity let $u,v:Q_B(X)\to Q_B(Y)$ have equal images under $H_{X,Y}$. By [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation] applied in $\mathcal B$, write them as roofs $(s_j:P_j\to X,a_j:P_j\to Y)$, $j=1,2$, with $s_j\in W_{\mathcal B}$. Their ambient roofs have equal images by step 3. By [lem-pc-right-fraction-common-refinement] in $\mathcal C$ there are $R$ and $b_j:R\to P_j$ such that $s_1b_1=s_2b_2\in W$ and $a_1b_1=a_2b_2$. Choose $r:B_R\to R$ in $W$ with $B_R\in\mathcal B$. Fullness makes $b_jr$ arrows of $\mathcal B$, while multiplicativity gives $s_1b_1r=s_2b_2r\in W_{\mathcal B}$ and $a_1b_1r=a_2b_2r$. The reverse implication of [lem-pc-right-fraction-common-refinement], now in $\mathcal B$ using steps 1-2, yields $u=v$. The arrows $b_j$ need not belong to $W$: only their common denominator and then its composite with $r$ do.

source.place: Tag 0GSL (lemma-localization-subcategory), categorical refinement argument; right-fraction axioms in Categories Tag 04VC (definition-multiplicative-system).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective] for $Q_B$, every object $A\in\mathcal L_B$ admits an isomorphism $e_A:Q_B(X_A)\xrightarrow{\sim}A$. Conjugation sends $u:A\to A'$ bijectively to $e_{A'}^{-1}ue_A$. Its image under $F$ is $F(e_{A'})^{-1}F(u)F(e_A)$. Thus the bijections on Hom sets established in steps 4-5 transport to every pair $A,A'$. Hence $F$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 0GSL (lemma-localization-subcategory), categorical refinement argument; right-fraction axioms in Categories Tag 04VC (definition-multiplicative-system).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective] for $Q_C$, every $D\in\mathcal L_C$ is isomorphic to $Q_C(X)$ for some $X\in\mathcal C$. Choose a denominator $s:B\to X$ with $B\in\mathcal B$. The composite $$F(Q_B(B))\xrightarrow{\alpha_B}Q_C(B)\xrightarrow{Q_C(s)}Q_C(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}D$$ is an isomorphism, since $Q_C$ inverts $W$. Hence $F$ is essentially surjective. Applying [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] with step 6 proves the claimed equivalence. No functorial choices of denominators, saturation of $W$, or triangulated structure entered the argument.
